page: Microsoft Azure F64as_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core topology on the x86_64 architecture, eliminating hyperthreading contention. Cache configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core alongside 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA_NI.

System memory consists of 256.0 GB RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage bundled with the allocation, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across single-core and multi-core computational tasks, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 30,887 and a PassMark CPU score of 114,813.89. Uncached memory throughput reaches 385.94 GB/sec for reads and 201.27 GB/sec for writes across large blocks.

In data operations and serving tasks, the instance achieves 168.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 95.49 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound machine learning benchmarks demonstrate competitive execution on small and medium models, reaching 5,645.59 prompt processing tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 61.5 text generation tokens per second on a 7B model. However, performance tapers on larger models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

The absence of integrated local storage necessitates external storage provisioning, which introduces architectural considerations for I/O path latency. Given its dense 64 dedicated core architecture, high memory bandwidth, and vector processing capabilities, Azure F64as_v7 is best fitted for continuous integration and compilation pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, in-memory caching tiers, CPU-based inference, and distributed batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure F64as_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 64 dedicated physical x86_64 cores without hyperthreading, the instance provides 256.0 GB of system memory at a 4.0 GB per-core allocation. It features advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring attached Premium Storage for disk operations, and includes no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place F64as_v7 in the top tier for multi-core computation, raw memory bandwidth, Redis transaction volume, and code compilation. The platform provides strong resource efficiency for compute-dense workloads that benefit from dedicated core isolation, making it suitable for distributed CI/CD builds, large-scale web tiers, in-memory caching layers, and CPU-driven mathematical modeling.
